toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The week of 26 Oct, at 0.41%, is inside the normal range. The 26 weeks before it averaged 0.354% with a top edge of 0.482%. Three earlier weeks were higher, and each was investigated with no fault found. Your policy says to note a week like this and take no action. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard isn't the cause: the raw logs recount to the same figures. Booking completion and support tickets didn't change.

The new-pod versus old-pod error gap seen during the rollout is not evidence against v4.18. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image. It comes from new pods starting with an empty cache and timing out on database fallbacks. It accounts for only 10–20 errors per rollout, against about 2,300 extra errors in the week.

I can't say whether the replica move or month-end partner-sync traffic added anything. The data doesn't need that answered to decide. Don't roll back, don't move the replica back, and don't mute alerting, which would remove your protection. Record the week as normal and run the standard check next week. If next week is above 0.482% or the burn-rate page fires, open an incident then.
